content.text: Good, small files clean so far. A few observations to hold: `sendBatchScheduleSms`/emails swallow all errors silently (only console.error, no Sentry) — worth flagging as medium. Now the reservations page and the two giant files.

Reservations page: mostly display-only, but the "Bill" button (line 833) and "Export"/"New Reservation" buttons have no `onClick` handlers — dead UI. Also `hours` sort field isn't in `SortField` union but `hours` exists on Reservation — not a bug since it's unused. Noting `handleSort`'s numeric sort is broken for non-string fields (cmp stays 0) but only string fields are sortable via UI, so low severity. Let's move to the huge files.

This is a massive file (23,664 lines, `Schedule()` alone spans ~11,500 lines). Let me focus on the conflict-detection and state-machine logic that's most likely to hide real bugs — the functions flagged by the task description: conflict detection, standby, maintenance sorting, drag targets.

I found an important bug candidate: `findScheduleMoveConflictForTargets` calls `doScheduleRangesOverlap` with only `{date, startHour, endHour}` for the target but passes the FULL `event` (line 2270) for the existing-event side. Let me check `doScheduleRangesOverlap` to see if that's a problem, and check `CONFLICT_IGNORED_STATUSES`.

This is fine — `doScheduleRangesOverlap` accepts anything with `date/startHour/endHour`, and `event` has those. That's fine (structural typing).

Now let's check `CONFLICT_IGNORED_STATUSES`, `NON_MOVABLE_EVENT_STATUSES`, and `STANDBY_SELECTABLE_EVENT_STATUSES` definitions, and `getScheduleMoveTargetsForDragState`'s snapping logic for edge cases across day boundaries.

Now the intra-batch conflict check (lines 2207-2230) checks pairwise overlap among the moving `targets` themselves, but doesn't filter by resource/status the way the second loop does — it just checks whether ranges overlap between ANY two selected targets, unconditionally, on the assumption all targets share the resource (since they're all snapped to `state.resourceId`). That's consistent. But this check doesn't skip status-ignored events — if two of the moved events are e.g. both `cancelled`/`standby` group-move, it'd flag a false conflict. But `isSelectableScheduleEvent` already filtered out `standby` unless `allowStandby`, and cancelled/completed/deleted are `NON_MOVABLE_EVENT_STATUSES` so excluded upstream.
